source:
# Port of lib/pubid/ieee/aiee/parser.rb — AIEE (pre-IEEE) designations:
# prefixes (IEEE-AIEE transitional, A.I.E.E. variants, AIEE), types
# (Standard No./Std No./Nos/No/Trans.), numbers (letters-dash, dotted,
# parenthetical alternates) and long/short dates. Consumed by the ieee
# grammar via `use aiee`. Deviation: source "Sep"/"Sept" order is
# lint-forced to longest-first.
#
# Edition-2 notes: the number capture inlines all five alternatives to
# raw terms, including the parenthetical-alternate branch — its
# main_number/alt_number/parenthetical sub-captures drop (a wrapper over
# them expands to element hashes, which cannot bind scalar; the old
# pipeline already flattened the subtree to the "431 (105)" span the
# capture now binds directly). The year body inlines at every capture
# site for the same reason; the digits rule inlines to 1*%x30-39 (a ref
# whose body is a repetition expands to node lists inside a capture).

grammar PubidAiee version "0.1.0" edition 2 {
  digit = %x30-39
  upper = %x41-5A
  lower = %x61-7A
  digits = 1*%x30-39
  space = " "
  dash = "-"
  dot = "."

  year = (("18" 2%x30-39)) / (("19" ("0" / "1" / "2" / "3" / "4" / "5") %x30-39)) / (("196" %x30-33))
  month_name = {
    "September"
    / "November"
    / "December"
    / "February"
    / "August"
    / "June"
    / "January"
    / "March"
    / "April"
    / "October"
    / "July"
    / "May"
    / "Sept"
    / "Jan"
    / "Feb"
    / "Mar"
    / "Apr"
    / "Jun"
    / "Jul"
    / "Aug"
    / "Sep"
    / "Oct"
    / "Nov"
    / "Dec"
  }
  aiee_prefix = ("IEEE-AIEE" / "A.I.E.E." / "A. I. E. E." / "AIEE") as publisher
  aiee_type = {
    (
      "Standard No."
      / "Standard No"
      / "Std No."
      / "Std No"
      / "Std"
      / "Nos"
      / "No."
      / "No"
      / "no"
      / "Standard"
      / "Trans."
    ) as type
  }
  number = {
    (
      ( 2*3%x41-5A "-" 1*%x30-39 )
      / ( 1*%x30-39 %x41-5A !( " and" ) )
      / ( 1*%x30-39 dot 1*%x30-39 )
      / ( 1*%x30-39 " (" 1*%x30-39 ")" )
      / ( 1*%x30-39 !( " and " 1*%x30-39 ) )
    ) as number
  }
  # The source's third date_long alternative (month dash year, no
  # separator) is dropped deliberately: under the edition-1 branch-commit
  # semantics the leading [space] commits before the alternation, so the
  # month-first form never matches ("AIEE No 15May-1928" and
  # "AIEE No 15 May-1928" both reject on the edition-1 artifact). Keeping
  # it would widen the accept set; month forms ride the separator
  # alternative, as on edition 1.
  #
  # The year body inlines at every capture site (a capture wrapping the
  # year rule ref expands to element hashes; the inline alternation binds
  # as one scalar string).
  date_long = {
    (
      ( [" "] ( ( ( "," / "." ) as separator ) [" "] [ ( month_name ) as month " " ]
          ( ("18" 2%x30-39)
            / ("19" ("0" / "1" / "2" / "3" / "4" / "5") %x30-39)
            / ("196" %x30-33) ) as year ) )
      / ( [" "] ( " -" ) as separator [" "]
          ( ("18" 2%x30-39)
            / ("19" ("0" / "1" / "2" / "3" / "4" / "5") %x30-39)
            / ("196" %x30-33) ) as year )
    )
  }
  date_short = {
    [" "] "-"
    ( ("18" 2%x30-39) / ("19" ("0" / "1" / "2" / "3" / "4" / "5") %x30-39) / ("196" %x30-33) ) as year
  }
  date = [(date_short / date_long)]

  aiee_identifier = aiee_prefix " " [aiee_type " "] number date

  entry aiee_identifier: aiee_identifier

  bindings aiee_identifier {
    publisher -> publisher (string)
    type -> type (string)
    number -> number (string)
    separator -> separator (string)
    month -> month (string)
    year -> year (string)
  }

  test {
    accept "AIEE No. 56"
    accept "AIEE Std 800"
    accept "IEEE-AIEE No 18-1938"
    accept "AIEE Standard 19"
    reject "nonsense"
  }
}
